subject: Discovery recap: Privacy & logging constraints for Acme Retail (next steps)
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2025-11-02T15:12:00-05:00
Subject: Discovery recap: Privacy & logging constraints for Acme Retail (next steps)

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the 40-minute intro today. Quick recap while it’s fresh and to confirm we’re aligned on pain, success criteria, and next steps.

Pain points you called out:
- Current in-house LLM gateway logs raw request/response to S3; compliance flagging PII stored in logs.
- No automated redaction pipeline; manual scrub is slow and brittle.
- Audit requests during promotions create heavy ad-hoc work for the infra team.

What you want to see / success criteria:
- Ability to prevent PII from being written to persisted logs (or automatically redact before persistence).
- Configurable retention windows (default 90 days, with ability to reduce to 30 days for certain collections).
- Exportable, tamper-evident audit logs for SOC2/PCI-style reviews.
- Clear mapping of where data flows (inference request -> cache -> logs -> S3/export).

Current stack notes you shared:
- AWS-hosted webapp + in-house inference gateway (Kubernetes) that writes structured JSON logs to S3.
- Security team manages KMS keys and a separate SIEM ingestion pipeline.

How Redwood can help (high level):
- Private deployment option in your VPC so logs and inference never leave your network control plane.
- Per-request policy hooks: can redact or mask before persistence, configurable per route.
- Audit logs with append-only export and HMAC signatures; retention lifecycle policy configurable.
- KMS/HSM support for key management and encryption in transit/at rest.

Attachments I’m including: redwood-security-overview.pdf (SOC2 + retention controls summary) and a mutual action plan template (MAP-template.xlsx) we can fill together.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll send the security overview + MAP (attached) — please share any gaps your security team needs in writing.
2) Schedule a focused demo for security/infra (we suggest a 45-minute walkthrough of Private deployment + redaction flows).
3) We’ll prepare a sample retention/config file and a short runbook that shows how logs are exported to your SIEM.
4) If this looks good, we’ll sync legal/ procurement timelines (you mentioned a target decision window of mid-December).

Can you confirm the best folks to include from Acme security (name/email), and whether the 45-minute demo on Nov 5th at 10am PT works?

Thanks —

Sean Gallagher
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.inference.com
+1 415-555-0123

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Privacy & logging constraints for Acme Retail (next steps)

Hi Sean —

Thanks for the concise recap — this matches our discussion. A couple of clarifications from Security:

- PII scope: customer name, email, shipping address, last4 card digits, and any free-text fields that may include contact info.
- Retention: baseline 90 days for activity logs, but marketing datasets must be purged at 30 days unless explicitly approved.
- Audit format: we need structured audit events (JSON) with event type, actor, timestamp, and non-repudiation metadata.

We can join the Nov 5th demo at 10am PT — I’ll add our security lead, Tom Keller (tom.keller@acmeretail.com), to the invite.

Before the demo, could you send a one-page example of: (1) an anonymization/redaction flow (what gets redacted when), and (2) sample audit event JSON? That will help our security and infra folks come prepared.

Regards,

Alice Nguyen
Product Ops — AI Integrations
Acme Retail

(415) 555-4420

Date: 2025-11-02T18:07:00-05:00
Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap: Privacy & logging constraints for Acme Retail (next steps)

Sean / Priyom —

Quick internal note on action items and recommended approach before the Nov 5th demo:

1) Deployment recommendation: propose Redwood Private in customer VPC with our logging disabled by default; only the audit export connector writes signed events to the customer S3 bucket. This keeps raw token-level output off persistent storage unless explicitly allowed.

2) Redaction options to show in demo:
   - Pre-persist redaction hook: configurable rules (regex + named-entity detection) that mask fields (email -> <REDACTED_EMAIL>, last4 -> XXXX).
   - On-write tokenization: replace sensitive spans with reversible tokens when customer enables HSM-backed tokenization.
   - Runtime transformations: a safe default that strips free-text outputs before they hit the log pipeline.

3) Audit log format: provide JSON schema that includes event_type, request_id, user_id (hashed), timestamp_iso, action, hmac_signature. We should prepare a sample JSON and an export example to their SIEM.

4) Docs & artifacts to attach to the demo invite: SOC2 report summary (redwood-security-overview.pdf), one-page redaction flow, sample audit event JSON, and the MAP-template.xlsx. Priyom — can you prepare the redaction flow + sample audit JSON by EOD tomorrow? I’ll own collating the SOC2 + product-runbook pieces.

5) Risk/ask for Legal: we may need a short DPA addendum covering log retention and deletion guarantees — flagging for legal to be ready if Acme requests.

Assigning:
- Priyom Das: demo script showing Private + redaction flows, sample audit JSON, staging config snippet.
- Monica Patel: security collateral and DPA checklist.
- Sean Gallagher: coordinate with Acme and confirm demo attendees & calendar.

If this approach sounds good I’ll draft the demo agenda and walkthrough order.

Monica
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.inference.com
